## Open

### T-386 — Mock get should attach the child arrays the real get builds

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · open_

A story Open page renders its read-only child lists empty: the real get answers the row plus its
child arrays (participations, campaigns, conferrals, attachments). The mock answers get from the
fixture row alone, so the athlete tabs show an empty table. Either the mock joins the related
fixture keys by foreign key, or the fixture grows a way to declare the sibling arrays; until then
the Playwright tab captures are the proof that the lists fill. Filed while writing the stories.

### T-395 — Derive personName so no producer can forget it

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · open_

The resource label of a person is personName, and every producer of a person has to supply it: the
regression, the registration flow and two seeds each build it by hand. Move the derivation into a
party handler that runs on add and edit so a caller that sends only the name parts still gets a
label.

### T-397 — Turn the rules.md acceptance criteria into automated tests

### T-399 — Cascade sport, discipline and category from the BOC nomenclature

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · open_

The reviewer asked for the three reference pickers to cascade: choosing a sport narrows the
disciplines, and choosing a discipline narrows the categories. The nomenclature itself has to come
from the Bulgarian Olympic Committee first — the codes and the parent-child pairs the real list uses
— so the discipline table needs a parent sport and the category table a parent discipline before any
dropdown can be filtered by the one above it. Implement the cascade with the widget parent option
once the data is known, and keep the independent pickers working for a record that has no sport yet.

### T-400 — Assert one resource row and a person with two roles

> _2026-10-23 · realm/blong-sport · open_

Section 12 of plans/sport/plan.md asks that add create exactly one person, one resource and one
profile row, and that a person with two roles end at two profile rows and one resource.
server/test/test/testAthlete.ts proves the person, the profile row and the shared id, but asserts
neither the resource row nor the second role, while profileRemove already refuses to delete a party
row another profile still holds. Extend the tap test with a resource count and with an athlete and a
coach created under one person id, then remove the athlete and expect the person and the resource to
survive.

### T-412 — Three sport browse shots are still unfiltered and empty

> _2026-10-25 · realm/blong-sport · done_

Three other browse shots in this realm are still unfiltered and are taken _before_ the spec creates
the row they could show: `organisations.play.ts` (federation) and `relationships.play.ts` (coaching,
support). They passed in CI because nothing else writes those tables, so a fresh database renders
`No rows.` — a deterministic but empty picture, and one that breaks the moment a seed or another
spec adds a row of that type. The fix is the one D-623 records for competition and campaign: move
the browse test after the create and pass `searchText` naming what it wrote, then re-capture the
baseline. Reading the browse page of an empty table also hides every column the model declares,
which is what a browse baseline is for.

Federation, coaching and support browse shots now create first and filter to their own row; all
three baselines re-captured and verified byte-identical across runs. D-623 extended.
